thread.title: Tech Today: Debating Cisco, Dropbox Versus Google, Liking Teradata

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Debating Cisco, Dropbox Versus Google, Liking Teradata
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated May 17, 2018 10:41 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Debating Cisco
Shares of Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) are down $1.45, or 3%, at $43.70, after the company yesterday afternoon slightly beat fiscal Q3 revenue and profit expectations, and forecast this quarter’s results more or less in line with consensus.
The company continues to make progress in transitioning its business to come from more recurring sources of revenue, and its “ campus ” switches for corporate networks returned to growth for the first time in several quarters, Chief Financial Officer Kelly Kramer told me in an interview .
For the bulls, Paul Silverstein of Cowen & Co. reiterates an Outperform rating, writing that the report is “ meaningfully better than [it] appears ."
“We think the reported numbers understate the true current and longer-term economics of CSCO’s business as measured by both growth and profitability—with ongoing improvement in the quality of CSCO’s earnings and cash flow to boot,” writes Silverstein.
In particular, he notes that the build-up in deferred revenue , from all those recurring sources, cut reported revenue growth by 2 to 2.5 percentage points.
"Of course, this near-term headwind will eventually transition to a tailwind—with the ongoing impressive build-up of deferred revenue eventually transitioning off of CSCO’s balance sheet into revenue on its income statement.
Among the bears, Tim Long of BMO Capital complains that the company’s amount of revenue from recurring sources, 32%, was down one percentage point from the prior quarter. He also notes that the company’s operating profit margin that it’s forecast this quarter, 29.5% to 30.5%, is two points less than he was expecting.
"An up-tick in opex is likely behind the weaker margin outlook, which we believe is associated with recent acquisitions,” writes Long.
Tesla’s Rising Capital Needs
Tesla ( TSLA ) might need a lot more money than people think.
Analysts have been generally saying the company will need to raise $2 billion to $3 billion this year, probably by the third or fourth quarter, even though CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly said the company doesn’t need to raise capital.
Goldman Sachs ’s David Tamberrino projects the company may need over $10 billion in financing come 2020 to fund current operations and to do things like building a new “gigafactory” in China. Tamberrino has a Sell rating on Tesla stock, and a $195 price target.
My colleague Teresa Rivas has more details about Tamberrino's note.
Tesla shares today are up 13 cents at $286.61.
Take-Two, Take Two
Shares of videogame maker Take-Two Interactive Software ( TTWO ), which owns the Rockstar Games brand, and Grand Theft Auto titles, among other things, are up $1.37, or 1.2%, at $114.44, reversing after-hours losses last night, after its fiscal Q4 revenue missed analysts' expectations , as did its outlook for revenue this quarter and for the full year.
Colin Sebastian with R.W. Baird , who has an Outperform rating on the stock, thinks Take-Two is feeling the pressure from "strong competition from Fortnite,” the free-to-play sensation that my colleague David Marino-Nachison has warned could hit the results of big gaming firms like Take-Two.
But many bulls are staying the course today. KeyBanc ’s Evan Wingren reiterates his Buy rating on the shares, and actually raises his price target to $152 from $144, writing that bears on the stock are inclined to "imply that you have to stretch RDR2 unit estimates to get upside,” referring to the company’s forthcoming Red Dead Redemption 2 game.
"We disagree,” writes Wingren, "and maintain that RCS [recurrent consumer spending, such as in-game purchases] and units have room for potential upside to guidance."
"In fact, it's hard to see what bears would play for in the near term given the 1Q weak guide, and that RDR2 unit risk is likely asymmetric to the positive side, in our view."
Teradata’s Less-Heavy Metal
Shares of venerable super-computing and Big Data firm Teradata ( TDC ) are up $1.77, or almost 5%, at $39.79, after Stifel ’s Brad Reback this morning raised his rating on the shares to Buy from Hold, and raised his price target to $49 from $45, lauding the company’s move away from selling dedicated hardware products to instead being a “ subscription-first ” business.
Reback thinks that Q1 was the first quarter where sales reps were “incentivized to sell subscription over licenses,” and that the push will ultimately "re-engage [Teradata] with its installed base,” thereby allowing it to "post healthy recurring revenue growth."
Pandora’s Stealth Transformation
Shares of streaming-music pioneer Pandora Media ( P ) are down 11 cents at $7.51, despite an upbeat note from Raymond James ’s Justin Patterson , who this morning reiterated a Strong Buy rating, after accompanying management to investor meetings , and coming away with good vibes "about the company’s strategy to improve audience trends and position the business for long-term growth."
"Broadly speaking, we believe Pandora’s progress has been under the radar ,” writes Patterson, "and investors are now rediscovering the music and audio discovery company."
"As new management continues to execute and metrics improve, we believe there is opportunity for multiple expansion."
PayPal Can Pay Big
Shares of payments pioneer PayPal Holdings ( PYPL ) are up 16 cents at $77.98, after Instinet ’s Bill Carcache reiterated a Buy rating, and raised his price target two bucks to $100, writing that he’s now expecting greater share repurchases , driving up his estimate for 2019’s earnings per share to $2.85 from his prior estimate for $2.81.
"PYPL’s buyback capacity is magnified by the strength of the cash on its balance sheet,” he writes, adding "we estimate that PYPL potentially has ~$21bn in liquidity at its disposal.” Carcache is looking forward to more details at the company’s May 24 analyst day meeting .
He’s mindful, however, that investors are “hungry” to hear how the company will “mitigate” the ending of its relationship with eBay ( EBAY ).
Dropbox Versus Google
Shares of recently pubic file-sharing service Dropbox ( DBX ) are down 6 cents at $30.68, after Deutsche Bank ’s Karl Keirstead this morning reiterated a Buy rating on the shares, telling investors not to be too worried about Alphabet’s ( GOOGL ) Google ’s new storage offering, “ Google One ,” which includes price cuts on large amounts of storage—$10 per month for two terabytes of storage, for example.
Keirstead sees a number of reasons why this isn’t a big threat to Dropbox, including that "Google is adding functionality for its own paying users, limiting the Dropbox displacement risk.” He muses this may be more about eating into Apple ’s ( AAPL ) iCloud appeal.
Plus, “If Google’s move is a response to demand for greater cloud storage capacity, it could be interpreted as a healthy signal for the overall market, although the downward price bias is a negative."
